name: Kitchen housewares department (customer). At store 92 'Kitchen' labels a shelf department — Appliances, Coffee Appliances/Blenders, Cookware/Food Processing/Mixers, Cookware Sets/Stockpots, Bake Ware/Dinnerware/Cutting Boards, Tabletop/Plasticware/Textiles/Pantryware plus the Kitchen Gadgets/Cutlery/Cutting Boards wall run — not a service counter. The derived auto:SEAFOOD disk (pt (1127,399), r=130, bridge 20) reaches back to x=997 and closed the 14-18 pt gaps between those shelf rows; the resulting pocket held the KITCHEN label, so the SERVICE_DEPTS substring cull condemned all 2206 cells as staff. Same false positive as 658/660's 'Kitchen Gadgets' aisle. East edge 1176 = the drawn shelf outline at x=1175; the 5 pt sliver between it and the wall at x=1182 stays sealed, as does the 6 pt crevice at y 374-378 between the department's south shelf row and the seafood counter (bottom edge stops at y=374 so that crevice cannot come back as an island).

Deli / Specialty Cheese customer frontage — the 22 pt (2.4 m) north-south corridor between the deli island's east face and the Kitchen shelf run, open at both ends (north past the Cooking Connection kiosk, south into the Sushiya/Bakery floor). The island itself (x 944-994, y 292-392) is a closed drawn polygon the extractor already blocks, so the staff side needs no exclusion; the DELI anchor (999.9,377) prints on this floor just off the island's south-east corner, which is why its window read only 47% walkable.

Bakery customer frontage — the BAKERY anchor (1029.5,485.7) prints on the shopping floor east of the drawn Tortilleria/bakery back-room wall (x=1010-1012 from y=430 to y=478), among the bakery display bins and the angled cases. Staff space here is that walled block west of x=1010, which the drawing already blocks, so the 100%-walkable VERIFY is a department name printed on the sales floor. North edge moved 470 -> 434 (audit 2026-07-27): the same shopping floor continues north to the back-room wall's corner at y=434 as a 12 pt alley between that wall (x=1006-1013) and the two bakery display bins (x=1026-1035, y 436-448 and 460-471), with the 10 pt gap between the bins linking it east to the open bakery floor. The auto:BAKERY disk bridged both ends shut and the whole alley was culled as a 138-cell dead crevice at (1021,453), leaving the bins' west and inner faces with no floor to stand on.

West end of the Baby cross-corridor (customer) — the 16 pt aisle between the Baby block's bottom shelf row (ends y=418) and the aisle-27 hair-care row (starts y=434); the Toddler/Infant Feeding, Baby Food, Baby Water and Baby Formula shelf labels print in it. The derived auto:PHARMACY disk (pt (322.7,534.4), r=130) reaches up to y=404 and bridged this corridor's west 110 pt shut, culling it as a 449-cell dead crevice at (337,423) even though the same corridor stays open east of x=400.

Produce display floor between the tables (customer) — the auto:BAKERY (1029.5,485.7) and auto:SEAFOOD (1127,399) disks both reach into Produce and bridged the 12-20 pt gaps around the Produce Station block, the small display tables and the wall cases, culling the walkway as six pockets (206 cells at (1094,565), 118 at (1078,541), 48 at (1045,593), 48 at (1083,593), 40 at (1091,508), 40 at (1091,526)). Every one of them is open produce floor a shopper stands on. The rect stops at x=1178/y=620, short of the perimeter sliver behind the south and east wall cases, which the drawing encloses and which stays sealed.

Seafood counter customer aisle (audit 2026-07-27) — the ~26 pt (2.8 m) diagonal aisle a shopper stands in to be served at the seafood counter and to shop the two angled seafood cases (drawn polys (1073.9,431)-(1094.8,437.1) and (1094.2,451.4)-(1115.1,457.4)). It is bounded north-east by the counter's own outer wall (x=1102 down to y=418, then a 45-degree face to (1133,441)) and south-west by those two cases. The auto:SEAFOOD disk (pt (1127,399), r=130) uses the wider SEAFOOD_BRIDGE of 20 pt, which closed the 15-20 pt mouths at both ends of the aisle and around the cases, culling it as three pockets (165 cells at (1103,435), 73 at (1106,469), 25 at (1067,422)). The shipped grid therefore had NO floor in front of the counter's service face and none on the display side of either case — 12 pt to the nearest standable cell mid-aisle — which is also why the SEAFOOD anchor far-snapped 13 cells (2.8 m). The exclusion's own text already asserts this aisle 'stays walkable'; this rect makes that true. The staff prep block behind the counter is the exclusion poly and stays sealed (free_raw is already false there, so an inclusion cannot reach it), and the 8 pt interior band between the counter's two drawn lines stays walled off by that outer line — walk_truth pins it at (1119,433). The shape is a poly, not a rect, because its north-east edge has to track that outer counter line (x = 1100 + (y-418) for y in 418..444): a rect square enough to hold the whole aisle also swallows the 12 pt counter band above y=430, which came back as a 34-cell island and split the uncut grid into two components.

Produce east wall-case frontage (audit 2026-07-27) — the floor a shopper stands on to shop the L-shaped wall case in the north-east corner of Produce (drawn poly (1145.3,446)-(1183.2,494.5)), whose six angled shelf fronts at x=1173-1176 face WEST into this pocket. The auto:SEAFOOD disk reaches here too (78 pt from its centre) and its 20 pt bridge closed the 15 pt gap between the case's north bar (ends y=454.5) and the free-standing bin at (1150.7,469.8)-(1159.1,485.4), culling 135 cells at (1163,468). The result was up to 2.36 m of dead floor directly in front of the case: only its bottom ~10 pt (y 486-494) had any frontage at all. No printed shelf label sits in the pocket, so neither coverage net could see it. East edge 1176 = the drawn case outline; the sliver between it and the wall at x=1183 stays sealed.
